DXC issue #2918 -- PIX numbering pass fails with /Od when subroutines are used
https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/issues/2918

READ THIS FIRST

This shader is a reconstruction written during triage. It is NOT the
shader in the report -- that one is private, referenced only by an
internal PIX bug number, and was never attached to the issue.

Compiler Explorer also cannot show the failure itself, for two
independent reasons:

  * the failure is in a PIX pass, which is not part of a dxc
    invocation. It runs afterwards, over an already-compiled module,
    through IDxcOptimizer::RunOptimizer -- what PIX does, and what
    dxopt.exe does from a command line. CE runs dxc only.
  * the oldest DXC on CE is 1.6.2112, which already contains the fix.
    The last release that reproduces is 1.5.2010.

So both panes here are expected to succeed. What they are for is the
debug metadata, which is the whole of the bug.

WHAT TO LOOK FOR

Scroll to the metadata at the bottom of either pane.

CullValues is a separate function in the source, and /Od keeps it as a
separate DISubprogram:

    !28 = !DISubprogram(name: "CullValues", linkageName: "\01?CullValues@@YAMV?$vector@M$02@@@Z", ...)

but its body ends up in @main. Every instruction that came from it
carries a !dbg whose scope is that subprogram -- and an inlinedAt:

    !78 = !DILocation(line: 18, column: 12, scope: !79, inlinedAt: !71)
    !79 = distinct !DILexicalBlock(scope: !28, file: !1, line: 18, column: 3)

inlinedAt: is the part that matters. Without it, a !dbg inside @main
whose scope chain ends at CullValues is illegal, and the LLVM verifier
rejects the module with

    !dbg attachment points at wrong subprogram for function

which is the assert in the report. Before the fix, the PIX
value-to-declare pass built its own DILocation from the variable's
declaration -- line, column 1, the variable's scope, and no inlinedAt --
and attached it to the llvm.dbg.declare it synthesised in @main. The
verifier that DxcOptimizer appends to the pass pipeline then failed the
whole RunOptimizer call, which is what surfaced in PIX as an exception.

The compare pane is another post-fix DXC; it is here to show the
metadata is stable, not to show a difference.
